questions.question_text: You are designing a new application that will be deployed across multiple AWS accounts and needs to monitor its performance, especially focusing on external dependencies. Which two services should you implement to ensure comprehensive monitoring and visibility into the application's behavior? (Select TWO)
options: A. Amazon S3 for storing logs from different accounts
B. AWS X-Ray to trace requests across services and identify bottlenecks
C. AWS CloudTrail for auditing API calls within each account
D. AWS Config to monitor the configuration of resources in each account
E. Amazon CloudWatch to set up custom metrics and alarms
questions.explanation:
A. INCORRECT: While S3 can be used for storing logs, it does not provide real-time visibility into application performance or external dependencies.

B. Correct: AWS X-Ray is essential for tracing requests across services and identifying bottlenecks in the application's behavior, especially when dealing with multiple accounts and external dependencies as mentioned in the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

C. INCORRECT: CloudTrail is used for auditing API calls but does not provide insights into application performance or external service dependencies.

D. INCORRECT: AWS Config monitors resource configurations but does not offer real-time monitoring of application performance or traceability across services.

E. CORRECT: Amazon CloudWatch can be set up to monitor custom metrics and set alarms, which is crucial for regularly monitoring the application's behavior and external dependencies as recommended in the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

Option A is too basic as it only sets up alarms without providing deeper insights into application behavior. Option C requires instrumenting existing services but can be done with minimal impact by selectively tracing requests. Option D, while useful for monitoring external APIs and services, can also be automated using AWS Lambda and CloudWatch Events to provide more comprehensive monitoring (AWS-Lambda.pdf, p.12; Amazon-CloudWatch.pdf, p.45).

questions.explanation:

This approach aligns well with the AWS Well-Architected Framework’s emphasis on cost optimization through efficient use of services like S3 and CloudFront.

Option A is suboptimal because deploying in a single region limits availability and does not address the need for a global user base. Option B uses Lambda functions, which are stateless and ideal for certain operations but would require RDS instances in each region, increasing costs and complexity unnecessarily. Option C, while providing high availability, may be more costly due to the use of EC2 instances and auto-scaling groups, which can have higher operational overhead compared to S3 and CloudFront.
